messages.subject: Importing R output into Open Office
messages.subject_clean: Importing R output into Open Office
messages.body_plain:
Just curious about something.

Often when I write a concordance script and import the results into Open Office, I encounter a row which contains what should be many different rows but which are all collapsed into one, generally bigger than the whole screen size, as if these lines were not encoded with sep="\n". What was a vector in R with a length of 500 might show up in Open Office as 450-or so lines of data. At first I thought it was some error in my script, but eventually I've come to suspect Open Office. Note that if I load the .csv file back into R, it works fine, each line a separate unit of data as intended. Yet in Open Office, the same lines get collapsed every time you open the csv.

Since this may happen to others (as it happens to me on different machines with different versions of Linux and using different scripts begun from scratch), there is work-around: copy the contents of the oversized row, paste into a text editor, then copy all of that and paste back into Open Office (checking the settings for separators because they're not the same as when importing files, nor does OOO remember previous choices).

But I'm just curious why this happens. Is it a quirk of Open Office as I suspect? Is it just Linux versions?

--
Kevin Parent, Ph.D, ACS, ALB
Korea Maritime University
Lt Governor of Education & Training, Korea Territorial Council (Toastmasters)
Schoolmasters: http://grou.ps/schoolmasters/
National Korea Toastmasters: http://grou.ps/koreatoastmasters

messages.subject: Combining Tables
messages.body_plain:
Is it possible to combine frequency tables?

For example:
Table One has, amongst many other words, THE with a frequency of 1000.
Table Two has THE with a frequency of 400.

How can I combine these into a single table that shows THE with a frequency of 1400 (and of course, all the other words combined as well).

--

Chair, Korea Toastmasters Territorial Council
